Subject: Uptime tranche & temporary credit waiver request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood’s latency and batch handling. Before we finalize procurement, our legal and ops teams asked if we could propose a short-term SLA adjustment for the onboarding window. Specifically: 

- Request: temporary baseline availability of 99.5% for the first 60 days from production go-live (we expect the first 6 weeks to include higher-than-normal traffic as we backfill KV caches).
- Credits: reduce the standard monthly credit tiers in that period to the attached tranche in edgesync_sla_matrix.xlsx; high-severity outages should still follow normal incident remediation.
- Cap: proposal includes a $30k monthly cap on credits while we ramp (see attachment).

I’ve attached a one-page mutual_action_plan.pdf that outlines the rollout milestones and our expected request curves. This is a hard requirement for our procurement team — they can’t accept a full 99.9 baseline during the initial ramp without limiting credit exposure.

Can your team confirm if Redwood can (a) agree to a 60-day temporary baseline at 99.5% and (b) accept a $30k cap on credits for that period, in exchange for a firm three-month usage commitment? If not, what alternatives do you recommend (shorter pilot window, staged caps, etc.)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to close this out.

Best,
Julia Chen
Head of SRE, EdgeSync Systems
julia.chen@edgesync.com

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the action plan. I’ve looped in Ben (sales) and Marissa (contracts) so we can evaluate both commercial and legal aspects. 

Quick take from my side (operational):
- Redwood’s standard public baseline is 99.9% availability.
- For ramp scenarios we typically offer a short-term pilot adjustment, but we prefer 30 days rather than 60 so we can verify telemetry patterns and validate KV/cache behavior.
- As a compromise, we can do a 30-day tranche at 99.5% with a staged credit cap: $30k for month 1, reviewed for month 2. That lets us limit exposure while giving EdgeSync runway.

I’m attaching our redwood_sla_template_v2.docx which contains the standard credit ladder and an internal amendment template we can use to formalize this pilot. If Ben confirms the commercial side (credits/cap), Marissa and I will run the amendment through our contracts queue.

If you need a 60-day window as a hard constraint, flag that explicitly and we’ll escalate, but it will likely require executive approval and an offset (either higher commit or a higher monthly fee).

Subject: Re: Uptime tranche & temporary credit waiver request — proposed credit schedule

Julia / Kimberly,

I’ve reviewed Julia’s request and Kimberly’s pilot suggestion. Commercially, here’s what I can put forward that balances EdgeSync’s need to limit credit exposure and Redwood’s need to protect long-run economics: 

Proposed temporary tranche (pilot period):
- Pilot length: 30 days (option to extend by mutual agreement).
- Availability baseline during pilot: 99.5%.
- Credit tiers during pilot: 
  * Availability >= 99.9%: no credit.
  * Availability >= 99.5% and < 99.9%: credit = 10% of monthly invoice for that month.
  * Availability < 99.5%: credit = 25% of monthly invoice, subject to a hard cap.
- Cap: proposal is $50k hard cap for the pilot month. If EdgeSync absolutely requires $30k, we can accept that on the condition of a 3-month committed volume or higher committed spend in month 1.

Additional notes:
- Latency SLAs: we typically do not put p95/p99 latency into the master SLA for pilot windows; recommend monitoring via the Redwood Console and adding latency guardrails into the success criteria of the mutual action plan.
- We can include a clause that allows a single one-time extension (to 60 days) if both sides agree, subject to executive sign-off.

I’m attaching credit_schedule.csv with the numeric examples and cap math. If EdgeSync can accept either (A) 30-day pilot + $50k cap, or (B) 60-day pilot + $30k cap but with a 3-month commit, we can move to contract redlines today.

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. Quick responses from EdgeSync: 

- We can accept the 30-day pilot as a first step. However, procurement prefers the certainty of a 60-day window before go-live for operational reasons (on-call handoffs, runbook validation).
- To bridge the gap: EdgeSync will agree to (A) a 60-day pilot at 99.5% if Redwood will accept a $30k cap for the first month and $40k for the second month, OR (B) a 30-day pilot with $30k cap in month 1 and a defined review to determine month 2 cap. Option A is our preference because it shortens approval cycles.
- We can offer the 3-month committed volume if needed; please provide the commitment threshold you’d need for the $30k fixed cap so we can confirm internally.

If we can get a redlined amendment today I can get legal to sign and route to DocuSign. I’ve attached the M.A.P. (mutual_action_plan.pdf) again for reference — it contains the telemetry/rollout milestones that will govern the review.

Would appreciate a one-hour slot tomorrow to finalize the language (I’m available 10–12 PDT).
